label: Creation Records
description: My Bloody Valentine's debut full-length trades their earlier jangle-pop for tremolo-bent, detuned guitars smeared into a single churning mass, with Bilinda Butcher and Kevin Shields' vocals buried as texture rather than lead instrument. It set the template — pitch-bending 'glide guitar,' whispered non-lyrics, drums mixed almost flat — that every shoegaze band after it copied. For listeners who want to hear the style before Loveless perfected it.
lineage: Grows out of Velvet Underground/Jesus and Mary Chain noise-drone (the V29 line) crossed with C86 jangle; leads directly to Loveless and the entire shoegaze/dream-pop vocabulary that countrygaze borrows textures from, not toward V29's deadpan songwriting side.

label: Creation Records
description: Loveless buries impossibly detuned, whammy-bar-warped guitars, cooing dual vocals and a hidden pop core under layers of tape manipulation and studio experimentation that reportedly bankrupted Creation Records. It is the field guide's canonical entry for the guitar-wall vocabulary — the 'noise wall' and 'harmonized guitars' descriptors — that countrygaze bands filter through pedal steel decades later. Essential listening for anyone tracing where the fuzz-and-drone side of the atlas gets its sonic palette.
lineage: The commercial and aesthetic peak of the C86/shoegaze branch off V29's drone lineage; its guitar-wall production directly informs the noise/slowcore Context lane and, at a distance, the pedal-steel-and-fuzz textures of Core countrygaze bands like Wednesday.

label: Creation Records
description: Slowdive slow their guitars down from My Bloody Valentine's roar into something closer to ambient music, with Neil Halstead and Rachel Goswell's voices floating over reverb-drenched chords and a Brian Eno co-write on 'Sing.' It softened shoegaze into dream pop proper and became the record most cited by 2010s revival bands. A key listen for hearing the gentler, more melodic half of the guitar-wall lineage.
lineage: Descends from the same C86/shoegaze branch of V29 as My Bloody Valentine but pushes toward ambient dream pop; that softer, glacial guitar tone echoes forward into slowcore and the hushed textures some countrygaze bands borrow.

label: Creation Records
description: Stripped almost entirely of drums and guitar riffs in favor of loops, drones and Talk Talk-style negative space, Pygmalion pushed shoegaze toward post-rock and got Slowdive dropped by Creation. It shows how far the 'guitar wall' idea could be dissolved into pure atmosphere. For listeners who already know Souvlaki and want the more experimental, ambient endpoint of the same band.
lineage: The most minimal extension of Slowdive's branch off V29's drone lineage, trading guitar-wall density for ambient space; anticipates the glacial, slow-build side of slowcore more than it feeds directly back toward twang.

label: Creation Records
description: Ride's debut balances shoegaze's guitar squall with clearer, more anthemic songwriting than My Bloody Valentine, letting choruses like 'Vapour Trail' cut through the haze. Andy Bell and Mark Gardener's twin vocals and the surging rhythm section made it one of the genre's most immediately catchy entries. A good landmark for hearing shoegaze's pop instincts alongside its noise.
lineage: Part of the same C86-into-shoegaze branch off V29 as My Bloody Valentine; its more melodic, jangle-inflected guitar wall points toward Britpop's guitar bands rather than back toward the Core's twang.

label: Creation Records
description: A cleaner, more confident follow-up to Nowhere, Going Blank Again opens with the widescreen 'Leave Them All Behind' and leans further into pop hooks without losing the guitar haze. It marked Ride's commercial peak in the UK before Britpop pulled the rug out from under shoegaze. Useful for tracing how the genre's guitar-wall vocabulary bent toward more conventional rock structure.
lineage: Continues Ride's branch off the C86/shoegaze line descending from V29; its arena-ready hooks show the guitar-wall aesthetic drifting toward mainstream British guitar rock rather than the DIY/Core lineage.

label: 4AD
description: Elizabeth Fraser's wordless, glossolalia-like vocals float over Robin Guthrie's chiming, reverb-soaked guitar and synth washes, defining the ethereal 4AD sound years before shoegaze proper existed. Treasure is the record most cited as dream pop's founding text and the clearest antecedent for the vocal-as-texture approach shoegaze bands adopted. A landmark for the 'cosmic' and 'hushed' end of the guitar-wall vocabulary.
lineage: An earlier, vocal-forward ancestor of the shoegaze branch off V29's drone lineage; its atmosphere directly shaped My Bloody Valentine and Slowdive's productions rather than descending from them.

label: 4AD
description: Cocteau Twins' most accessible record brings Elizabeth Fraser's vocals higher in the mix and closer to actual (if still oblique) lyrics, wrapped in warm, chiming guitar and synth arrangements. It became the gateway album for listeners intimidated by the band's earlier, more abstract work. A useful contemporary counterpart to My Bloody Valentine's Loveless, showing the softer, more melodic end of the same scene.
lineage: Sits alongside Slowdive and Lush in the dream-pop wing of the shoegaze branch off V29; its melodic clarity influenced later dream-pop and indie-pop rather than feeding the noisier Core-adjacent lanes.

label: Taang! Records
description: Recorded on a shoestring budget with Sonic Youth's tunings and My Bloody Valentine's guitar haze filtered through American college-rock scrappiness, Blonder Tongue Audio Baton splices tape loops, drum-machine interludes and sudden noise collages between its pop songs. It is the American shoegaze scene's defining record and a direct forerunner of the lo-fi, guitar-wall indie that later feeds countrygaze's noisier edges. A field-guide-cited landmark for the U.S. side of the genre.
lineage: Transplants the UK shoegaze branch of V29 into the Boston DIY/college-radio network (the same network that feeds SST/lo-fi indie); its noisy, tape-collaged version of the guitar wall is a direct ancestor of American slowcore and noise-pop rather than the UK dream-pop line.

label: 4AD
description: Produced by Robin Guthrie of Cocteau Twins, Spooky pairs Miki Berenyi and Emma Anderson's close harmonies with thick, chorused guitar layers that sit between shoegaze fog and dream-pop clarity. It shows the genre's female-fronted, 4AD-adjacent wing distinct from the male-led Creation bands. A solid landmark for the harmony-heavy side of the guitar-wall vocabulary.
lineage: Another 4AD-rooted branch off V29's shoegaze/dream-pop lineage, produced by a Cocteau Twins member; its close-harmony vocal approach echoes forward into later dream-pop and twee-adjacent indie pop.

label: Dedicated Records
description: Chapterhouse blend shoegaze guitar fog with dance-influenced rhythms and drum machines, reflecting the early-90s crossover between indie and rave culture ('Madchester' adjacent). Whirlpool is a solid mid-tier landmark showing shoegaze's willingness to absorb electronic production. Good for hearing a less guitar-orthodox branch of the same scene as Ride and Slowdive.
lineage: A Reading-scene sibling of Ride within the shoegaze branch off V29; its electronic leanings point toward 90s indie-dance crossover rather than back into the Core's acoustic-and-twang lineage.

label: Dedicated Records
description: Chapterhouse's second and final album pushes further into shimmering, synth-inflected guitar pop as shoegaze's UK commercial moment was closing. It rounds out the picture of the genre's more melodic, dance-adjacent wing before Britpop swept it aside. A deeper cut for completists mapping the scene's final wave.
lineage: The tail end of Chapterhouse's branch off V29's shoegaze lineage, released as the UK press turned toward Britpop; its dance-pop instincts fed forward into 90s electronic-indie crossover rather than back toward twang.

label: 4AD
description: Pale Saints' debut mixes jangly, Byrds-indebted guitar lines with sudden bursts of shoegaze noise and Ian Masters' airy vocals, sitting between the 4AD dream-pop catalog and the louder Creation bands. It is a lesser-known but well-regarded landmark that shows the stylistic range within the scene. A good pick for listeners who want the jangle-into-noise version of shoegaze.
lineage: A 4AD-scene branch off V29's shoegaze lineage that keeps more jangle-pop clarity than My Bloody Valentine; its melodic guitar interplay anticipates later British indie guitar bands rather than the Core's country side.

label: 4AD
description: With new member Meriel Barham (ex-Lush) sharing vocals, In Ribbons leans further into dream-pop melody while keeping the debut's noisier textures in reserve. It is a solid second landmark for a band often overshadowed by its 4AD labelmates. Recommended for filling out the roster beyond the genre's best-known names.
lineage: Continues Pale Saints' branch off V29's dream-pop/shoegaze lineage with a lineup change that ties it to Lush; the record's melodic focus feeds forward into 90s British indie pop rather than back toward the Core.

label: Harvest Records
description: Wire strip punk down to blunt, angular fragments — 21 songs in under 36 minutes, several barely a minute long — replacing Ramones-style buzz with clipped riffs, deadpan vocals and abrupt stops. It is the founding document of art-punk's move into post-punk, endlessly cited by Minor Threat, R.E.M. and Elastica alike. The essential landmark for the rhythmic, angular line adjacent to the scene.
lineage: Splits off V29's art-punk deadpan and the punk foundation of X14 into a more clipped, structurally radical post-punk; its influence runs forward through Minor Threat and Fugazi's DIY rigor rather than toward twang or country.

label: Harvest Records
description: Wire's second album opens up the terse songs of Pink Flag into longer, synth-and-effects-laden arrangements, edging toward the atmospheric side of post-punk without losing its angularity. It shows the band already restless with the sound they had just invented. A strong second landmark for hearing post-punk's rapid evolution.
lineage: Continues Wire's branch off X14/V29 into more textured, synth-inflected post-punk; its atmosphere influenced the goth and art-rock wings of the genre rather than the twangier Core lineage.

label: Harvest Records
description: Named for the number of shows the band had played, 154 pushes furthest into studio experimentation and melodic ambition before Wire's late-70s lineup fractured. It closes out the trilogy that made Pink Flag, Chairs Missing and 154 foundational post-punk texts. A deeper cut for listeners already sold on the first two records.
lineage: The final entry in Wire's initial branch off X14/V29's post-punk lineage before a long hiatus; its polish anticipated 80s art-rock production more than the DIY roughness that fed the American noise-rock wing.

label: Ace of Hearts Records
description: Mission of Burma's only studio album from their original run pairs blaring, tape-loop-treated guitar squall with tightly wound rhythms and Roger Miller and Clint Conley's alternating shouted vocals. It became a foundational text for American noise-rock and post-hardcore despite selling few copies at the time. Essential for the angular, rhythmic line that runs from Boston's scene through Fugazi and beyond.
lineage: An American, Boston-scene branch off X14's punk foundation and V29's art-noise lineage; its tape-loop noise and structural aggression directly informed Sonic Youth, Hüsker Dü and the noise-rock wing of X10 rather than any twang-adjacent lane.
key_tracks: That's When I Reach for My Revolver

label: Matador Records
description: Reuniting after a 20-year hiatus, Mission of Burma sound barely diminished on ONoffON, matching Vs.'s aggression with slightly cleaner production and Bob Weston (of Shellac) replacing original tape-loop manipulator Martin Swope. It proved the band's reunion was substance over nostalgia. A useful modern example of the lane's founders still working.
lineage: A late-career continuation of Mission of Burma's original branch off X14/V29's noise-punk lineage, with a Shellac/Big Black connection tying it to the Chicago noise-rock wing of the same lane.

label: Homestead Records
description: Steve Albini's Big Black replace a drummer with a programmed Roland drum machine and pair it with clanging, treated guitars and confrontational lyrics about violence and small-town rot. Atomizer is the genre-defining noise-rock record, mechanical and abrasive where Mission of Burma is loose and shouted. A must-hear landmark for the harder, industrial-adjacent end of the post-punk/noise-rock line.
lineage: Splits from X14's hardcore roots into a colder, drum-machine-driven noise rock distinct from Wire or Mission of Burma's more melodic post-punk; Albini's engineering work afterward directly shaped the Pixies, Nirvana and much of 90s indie production.

label: Touch and Go Records
description: Big Black's second and final studio album sharpens Atomizer's clanging drum-machine noise rock with even more caustic production and a cover of Kraftwerk's 'The Model' rendered as pure menace. It closed out the band before Albini moved fully into producing other artists' records. A strong second landmark for the noise-rock wing of the lane.
lineage: The endpoint of Big Black's branch off X14's punk lineage before Albini's influence shifted from performing to producing; its scorched-earth sound directly informed Shellac and the broader 90s noise-rock underground.

label: Dischord Records
description: Fugazi's first full-length turns Ian MacKaye's hardcore background and Guy Picciotto's more melodic instincts into tense, dub-influenced post-hardcore built on stop-start dynamics and pointedly political lyrics. Repeater made the band's DIY ethics (five-dollar shows, no merch markup) as influential as its music. The essential landmark for the DIY-network end of the rhythmic, angular line.
lineage: Grows out of X14's hardcore-punk roots (MacKaye's earlier Minor Threat) filtered through V29's art-rock structural sense; Fugazi's DIY model directly fed the SST/college-radio network (the same trunk line that runs into lo-fi indie and the Core).

label: Dischord Records
description: A heavier, more abrasive record than Repeater, In on the Kill Taker was partly re-recorded with Steve Albini before the band finished it themselves, resulting in some of Fugazi's most aggressive material. It shows the post-hardcore/noise-rock overlap within the lane at its most direct. A strong second landmark for the band's catalog.
lineage: Continues Fugazi's branch off X14/V29 with a direct Albini connection tying it to the noise-rock wing of the same lane; its aggression influenced 90s post-hardcore more than any twang-adjacent lineage.

label: Dischord Records
description: Fugazi loosen their sound on Red Medicine, adding studio experimentation, quieter passages and even a clarinet solo alongside the usual tense dynamics, recorded and self-produced entirely on their own terms. It shows a band expanding past hardcore's constraints while keeping its DIY politics intact. Recommended for hearing the band's mid-career evolution.
lineage: A later, more experimental branch off Fugazi's X14/V29 post-hardcore lineage; its loosened structure anticipated post-rock's use of dynamics more than it fed back toward the lane's noisier origins.

label: Hardly Art
description: Joe Casey's world-weary, half-spoken baritone narrates Rust Belt decay and municipal corruption over Greg Ahee's needling, repetitive guitar lines, updating Wire and Fall-style post-punk for post-recession Detroit. It is the modern touchstone for the lane's angular, rhythmic vocabulary translated into American indie rock. A good example of a current band still working directly in Wire's tradition.
lineage: A modern American continuation of the post-punk branch off X14/V29, closer to the Fall's deadpan delivery than to noise rock's abrasiveness; feeds today's post-punk revival (Idles, Shame) rather than the Core's twang.

label: Domino
description: Protomartyr's fourth album widens its scope to post-truth politics and mortality, with Casey's lyrics sharper and the band's arrangements more expansive than on earlier records, released on the larger Domino label. It marked the band's critical breakthrough beyond the post-punk revival's cult audience. Recommended as a second, more polished entry point.
lineage: Continues Protomartyr's modern branch off X14/V29's post-punk lineage with a bigger production budget; its political storytelling parallels Southern-gothic songwriting elsewhere in the atlas without ever crossing into twang.

label: Saddle Creek
description: Indigo De Souza's second album swings between shredded-throat pop-punk catharsis and glossy synth interludes, with songs about grief, queerness and self-destruction delivered with disarming directness. She is placed here on a scene-not-sound ruling: she is a central figure of the Asheville DIY community that also produced MJ Lenderman and Wednesday, but her sound is punk/pop-punk rather than countrygaze. Included as a Context landmark for that Asheville connective tissue.
lineage: Not a sonic descendant of the post-punk canon above; included in X10 because her music runs angular and punk-adjacent rather than twangy, and because she shares the Asheville scene (not the sound) with Core artists like Wednesday and MJ Lenderman.
borderline_note: Scene-not-sound placement per assignment ruling: Asheville DIY-scene peer of Core artists, but punk/pop-punk sound, not countrygaze.

label: Fire Talk Records
description: Robber Robber's Fire Talk debut hits harder and more explosively than the Burlington quartet's earlier work, pairing thick, distorted guitars with tightly coiled, start-stop arrangements closer to noise rock than to twang. They are placed here on a scene-not-sound ruling, tying them to Vermont's small but tight-knit DIY guitar-band scene. A modern example rounding out the lane's contemporary edge.
lineage: Not a direct sonic descendant of classic post-punk; included in X10 because their noisy, angular guitar rock fits the lane's sound while their real connection to the wider atlas is scene (Burlington, VT DIY) rather than genre lineage into twang.
borderline_note: Scene-not-sound placement per fieldguide_mapping.csv: Burlington, VT DIY-scene band, punk/noise-rock sound, not countrygaze.

label: Southern Ground
description: Produced by Zac Brown, The Whippoorwill is Blackberry Smoke's commercial and critical breakthrough, pairing triple-guitar boogie and pedal steel flourishes with radio-ready choruses about hard living and the open road. It represents Southern rock's mainstream 2010s revival at its most confident. Essential listening for hearing where the Skynyrd/Allman lineage lands as arena-country-rock today.
lineage: Carries V28's Skynyrd/Allman/Marshall Tucker Southern-rock guitar lineage into 2010s mainstream rock and country-adjacent radio, heading toward jam-band and classic-rock revivalism rather than the punk-inflected storytelling that produced Drive-By Truckers and the Core.

label: Rounder Records
description: Blackberry Smoke's Rounder Records debut hit number one on Billboard's country albums chart, cementing the band's crossover between rock radio and Nashville without softening its boogie-rock core. It shows Southern rock's mainstream continuation reaching genuine chart success rather than nostalgia-circuit status. A solid second landmark for the band's arc.
lineage: Continues Blackberry Smoke's branch off V28's Southern-rock lineage into commercial country-rock crossover; its chart success illustrates how far this line drifted from the Core's indie/DIY route.

label: 3 Legged / Thirty Tigers
description: Co-produced by Dave Cobb, You Hear Georgia leans into big, radio-friendly hooks (including a title track featuring Warren Haynes and Jamey Johnson) while keeping the band's triple-guitar Southern-rock foundation intact. It shows the band still drawing A-list Southern-music collaborators well into its third decade. A strong recent example of the lane's continuing mainstream presence.
lineage: A recent entry in Blackberry Smoke's ongoing branch off V28's Southern-rock lineage, produced by Dave Cobb, whose work elsewhere ties the mainstream and Americana wings of Southern music together without pulling this record into the Core.

label: Wiggy Thump Records
description: Firewater is the East Texas band's breakout, mixing Skynyrd-style twin-guitar riffing with outlaw-country grit and Cody Cannon's rough-edged drawl on songs about drinking, hard times and small-town life. It established Whiskey Myers as a leading voice of the 2010s Southern-rock revival alongside Blackberry Smoke. Essential for hearing the Texas variant of the lane's sound.
lineage: Extends V28's Skynyrd/Allman Southern-rock guitar lineage through a Texas outlaw-country filter, heading toward mainstream Red Dirt/Southern-rock touring circuits rather than the indie-twang Core.

label: Wiggy Thump Records
description: Early Morning Shakes sharpens Whiskey Myers' twin-guitar attack and adds tighter songwriting, expanding the band's audience beyond the Texas/Red Dirt circuit. It is a strong second landmark showing the band's steady climb through the 2010s Southern-rock revival. Recommended as a companion to Firewater.
lineage: Continues Whiskey Myers' branch off V28's Southern-rock lineage into a wider national touring audience, still oriented toward mainstream rock radio rather than the Core.

label: Wiggy Thump Records
description: Mud pairs Whiskey Myers' Skynyrd-indebted riffing with more polished, radio-ready production, becoming the band's first top-10 entry on the Billboard 200. It marks the point where the Southern-rock revival broke into genuine mainstream visibility. A useful landmark for the lane's commercial peak.
lineage: A commercially peaking entry in Whiskey Myers' branch off V28's Southern-rock lineage, illustrating the lane's arrival at mainstream rock-radio and streaming success rather than the DIY/indie route.

label: Wiggy Thump Records
description: The self-titled fifth album broadens Whiskey Myers' palette with horns, gospel-tinged backing vocals and slower, more reflective songs alongside the usual boogie-rock riffing. It shows a Southern-rock band mid-career trying to stretch past genre expectations without abandoning them. Recommended for hearing the band's most ambitious studio work.
lineage: A more expansive, horn-and-gospel-inflected entry in Whiskey Myers' branch off V28's Southern-rock/soul lineage, still aimed at mainstream rock audiences rather than the Core.

label: BMG
description: Formed by the sons of three founding Allman Brothers Band members (Devon Allman, Duane Betts, Berry Duane Oakley), the Allman Betts Band's debut recreates the twin-lead-guitar, jam-friendly sound of their fathers' band almost note for note, down to a title track that echoes 'Blue Sky.' It is the most literal possible continuation of Southern rock's original lineage into the present. Essential for showing the mainstream continuation as a direct family inheritance.
lineage: A direct, literal continuation of V28's Allman Brothers lineage carried by the founders' own children; heads toward legacy-act jam-band touring rather than the twangier, punk-inflected Southern storytelling of the Core.

label: BMG
description: Bless Your Heart stretches into longer, more improvisational arrangements than the debut, closer to the Allman Brothers' live-jam tradition, and was recorded partly at the Muscle Shoals Sound Studio. It doubles down on the band's role as caretakers of their fathers' sound rather than pushing toward reinvention. Recommended as a second, jammier landmark.
lineage: Continues the Allman Betts Band's direct-inheritance branch off V28, leaning further into the jam-band side of Southern rock rather than toward the Core's more compact songwriting.

label: Thirty Tigers
description: The Steel Woods' debut fuses heavy, Skynyrd-and-Zeppelin-indebted riffing with outlaw-country songwriting and a cover of David Allan Coe's 'If That Ain't Country,' positioning the Nashville band between Southern rock and heavier Americana. Guitarist Jason 'Rowdy' Cope's death in 2021 cut the band's run short, making this an important document of the lane's harder-rocking wing. Essential for the heavier, storytelling-forward branch of modern Southern rock.
lineage: Extends V28's Southern-rock lineage through a heavier, Waylon-and-Skynyrd-citing outlaw-country filter, closer to the Core's storytelling instincts than most of this lane but still landing in mainstream rock/Americana touring rather than indie twang.

label: Thirty Tigers
description: Old News keeps The Steel Woods' heavy riffing intact while sharpening the band's storytelling on songs about addiction, mortality and hard-won faith, recorded not long before Jason Cope's death. It is a strong second landmark showing the band's growth as writers within the genre. Recommended as a companion to the debut.
lineage: A continuation of The Steel Woods' branch off V28's Southern-rock lineage with deepening Americana songwriting, still oriented toward mainstream rock/Americana audiences rather than the Core.

label: Tricki-Woo Records
description: Sisters Rebecca and Megan Lovell push their roots-rock sound toward heavier blues-rock on Venom & Faith, built around slide guitar, stomping rhythms and reworked blues and gospel standards alongside originals. It shows a related mainstream continuation of Southern guitar-rock filtered through blues rather than boogie-rock radio. Recommended for the slide-guitar, blues-rock branch of the lane.
lineage: A blues-rock-leaning branch off V28's Southern guitar-rock lineage (via the Allman Brothers' slide-guitar tradition specifically), heading toward the contemporary blues-rock circuit rather than the punk-adjacent Core.

label: Tricki-Woo Records
description: Blood Harmony won the 2024 Grammy for Best Contemporary Blues Album, pairing the Lovell sisters' close harmonies and slide-guitar riffing with the band's most polished, arena-scaled production yet. It represents the commercial high point of the blues-rock wing of Southern rock's mainstream continuation. A strong recent landmark for the lane.
lineage: Continues Larkin Poe's branch off V28's Southern slide-guitar lineage into Grammy-recognized mainstream blues-rock, distinct from both the boogie-rock (Blackberry Smoke) and jam-band (Allman Betts) wings of the same lane.
